name: A narration in the world, and an ambient sound near it

lines.text: You are standing where the town well stood for three hundred years.
Every morning the square filled with people carrying buckets, and news.
In dry summers a guard sat here, so that nobody took more than their share.
When water pipes reached the houses in 1902, the well was covered over.
The ring of paving stones around you still marks its edge.
Look down: the darker stones in the middle are the old well head.
Walk on toward the market, and listen to it as you go.

longest.title: The weavers' guild house and the long quarrel over the market hall roof, 1612-50

lines.text: In the spring of 1612 the weavers' guild, which had grown rich on the wool trade along the river, asked the town council for permission to build a second floor above the open market hall, so that its members could meet, store their cloth and keep their accounts under one roof.
The council agreed, but the butchers, who sold their meat in the hall below, refused to pay for a new roof that would mostly serve the weavers.
The quarrel went on for almost forty years, through two fires, a flood and a war, and it was settled only when both guilds had run out of money.
The roof you see today is the one they finally agreed on in 1650.
